info.name: firecrawl-integration-test
info.description:
Examples for the local Docker Compose Firecrawl stack, configured with a local Open APi LLM backend. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-11-local-docker-lmstudio-design.md for setup context.

No auth headers needed against {{baseUrl}} — USE_DB_AUTHENTICATION=false in .env for this local stack.

request.description: Should return 200 with no body when the api container is up.
No LLM involved — pure fetch + markdown conversion. Good smoke test that doesn't depend on Open APi.

Routes the extraction through OPENAI_BASE_URL (Open APi) via Chat Completions. Local models are slow — expect ~15-30s. Response should have data.json.heading populated; if data.json is missing, check the api container logs for a coerceFieldsToFormats warning (schema mismatch) and cross-check Open APi's server log.
Fast link discovery, no LLM/scrape involved. Good for testing the stack without waiting on Open APi.
Kicks off an async crawl job and auto-saves the returned id into the {{crawlId}} collection variable for the next request.
Run 'Start Crawl' first to populate {{crawlId}} automatically, or set it manually.

item.name: Extract (deprecated, uses Gemini not Open APi)

request.description: Firecrawl marks /v1/extract deprecated in favor of /v2/scrape. Its reranker (lib/extract/reranker.ts) is hardcoded to Gemini and does NOT route through Open APi — requires GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY to be set, falls back gracefully (logs a warning, returns empty relevance list) if that key is weak/missing rather than failing the whole request. Expect ~40-60s.

item.name: Search Safe Filter (Jev via OpenCode Zen)
item.description: Exercises Jev (TypeSafe) through /v2/search safe:true. lib/search/safe-search.ts asks Jev one noul question per result and drops anything scoring above 0.3. Needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY in .env, forwarded into the container by x-common-env, plus TYPESAFE_MODEL (e.g. jev-1.13 on OpenCode Zen). The last two requests run the same filter at limit 20: the page-size contract (cost, latency, one noul question per result) and the over-filtering guard.

item.description: Guards the opposite failure: Jev over-filtering. The upstream search provider is intermittent, so the query is retried for up to 60s. If it still returns nothing there is nothing for Jev to have judged, so the request is SKIPPED instead of failing - an empty result set is a provider outage, not a Jev defect. The strict check, when results do come back, is that no explicit URL survived.

item.name: Twenty results through the safe filter

request.description: The same call as the rest of this folder at four times the size. The point of limit 20 is cost and shape, not filtering: removeExplicitResults (apps/api/src/search/safe-search.ts) asks Jev one noul question per result, so a page of 20 is 20 Zen calls and the slowest part of the request. Watch the response time against the limit 5 example - SearXNG pages 20 at a time, so this is also the first size where Firecrawl needs more than one page.

item.name: SearXNG (local search provider)
item.description:
SearXNG is the container /v2/search asks first on this stack. The chain is fire-engine -> SearXNG -> DuckDuckGo (apps/api/src/search/v2/index.ts); with FIRE_ENGINE_BETA_URL unset, SearXNG is the first link and DuckDuckGo only fills in what it missed. Two halves: the first talks to the instance directly, which is how you tell a SearXNG problem apart from a Firecrawl problem; the second goes through Firecrawl and asserts the shape apps/api/src/search/v2/searxng.ts builds.

Knobs: SEARXNG_ENDPOINT in .env (without it Firecrawl never calls SearXNG at all), SEARXNG_ENGINES / SEARXNG_CATEGORIES to narrow the web category, SEARXNG_NEWS_CATEGORIES to replace the news categories (default news), and searxng/settings.yml, which must keep search.formats [html, json] - without json Firecrawl gets 200 responses carrying no results array.

{{searxngUrl}} is a collection variable so these run without an environment change; point it at the SEARXNG_ENDPOINT host.

The folder carries one pre-request guard: a request whose host variable does not resolve to a real URL is skipped with a console warning naming the variable, which is what a shared-link copy (no collection variable, no environment selected) produces.

item.name: Through Firecrawl (/v2/search)
item.description: The same SearXNG instance as seen by a Firecrawl caller: categories mapped per source, results reshaped by the mappers. Note what these cannot prove - the DuckDuckGo fallback produces the same url/title/description fields, so a passing response here does not by itself prove SearXNG answered. Run the Standalone folder when you need to know that.
